title: Microsoft Copilot: Agent Mode in PowerPoint builds presentations from Work IQ
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves Work IQ billing and SharePoint discovery protection uncertain even though Microsoft's general rules cover this licensed Copilot experience. It also attributes an unspecified Work IQ switch to administrators and overstates licence assignment as controlling every route to Work IQ.

## July 01, 2026
**Roadmap ID:** 555874
Copilot in PowerPoint now uses Work IQ to automatically gather relevant files, meetings, and emails to help build presentations.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn names no separate licence specific to Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent Mode" "PowerPoint" "Work IQ" default licensing admin; "PowerPoint" "Work IQ" "Copilot Credits" pricing license. Read release notes, Copilot overview, Work IQ overview and pricing search results; no separate feature-specific licence or price.

claims.claim: Whether Agent Mode in PowerPoint draws on the Work IQ API meter is not stated.
claims.quote: Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), whereas the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering that can be purchased and consumed independently for custom apps, agents, and integrations.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery needs Copilot licensing and available SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits SharePoint content discovery in Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as a temporary governance control while access is reviewed.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The control's documentation describes Copilot discovery generally without naming Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn covers Microsoft Copilot discovery generally and does not name Agent Mode in PowerPoint' in the row note with 'Applies to Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.' Retain the exception for content already in use.

claims.claim: Whether Restricted Content Discovery governs this feature's Copilot discovery boundary remains an open question.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.fix: Replace the prose caveat with 'Restricted Content Discovery applies to Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery; it does not affect experiences on content already in use, such as summarising an open document.' In the final open question, remove 'Does Agent Mode in PowerPoint use the same discovery boundary that Restricted Content Discovery sets for Microsoft Copilot, and' so it asks only about sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot overview says an administrator can turn Work IQ on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" administrator "turn" "off" "Copilot responses"; "Work IQ" "on or off" admin PowerPoint. Read Copilot overview and Work IQ API tenant setup; overview says 'You can turn Work IQ on or off' without specifying an administrator or an admin control.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn's Microsoft Copilot overview says an administrator can turn Work IQ on or off' with 'Learn's Microsoft Copilot overview says Work IQ can be turned on or off, without identifying the setting or who controls it.' Do not attribute the API setup, MCP policy or Business Applications controls to this in-PowerPoint setting.

claims.claim: When Work IQ is off, Copilot responses are not grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.quote: When Work IQ is off, Copilot responses aren't grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.

claims.claim: Licence assignment decides who can use Work IQ at all.
claims.quote:
Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.
claims.fix: Replace 'Licence assignment decides who can use Work IQ at all' with 'Licence assignment controls entitlement to Work IQ grounding included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium); Work IQ API access is independent of that licence and is usage-based.' Cite the already listed Work IQ overview.

claims.claim: Any over-permissioned site or mailbox feeds slides.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint"; "PowerPoint" "Work IQ" "Restricted Content Discovery". Read release notes, Copilot privacy and Restricted Content Discovery; they describe relevant authorised retrieval, not guaranteed inclusion of every accessible site or mailbox.
claims.fix: Replace 'so any over-permissioned site or mailbox feeds slides' with 'so existing oversharing can make sensitive source material available to Copilot when it gathers relevant content.' This preserves the risk analysis without claiming that every accessible source is used.
